children.translated_text: Therefore the <s>nāḍīyantra</s> instruments, connected with the staraṇa-site, are hollow in the middle like tubes.

children.text: āgantukāraṇe mānase ca kathaṃ vātādimūlatvamityāha talliṅgatvāditi vātādiliṅgayuktatvādityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Regarding an adventitious cause and a mental one, how can there be rootedness in <s>vāta</s> (wind humor) and the other <s>doṣa</s>s (pathogenic factors)? He says, "because they have their signs"; that is, because they are furnished with the signs of <s>vāta</s> and the others.

children.text: āgantāvapi hi vātādiliṅgaṃ śarīrakṣobhādavaśyaṃ bhavati paraṃ tat kiyantamapi kālaṃ vātādicikitsāprayojanakaṃ na bhavati yaduktaṃ tatrābhighātajo vāyuḥ prāyo raktaṃ pradūṣayan ityādi ||
children.translated_text: For even in an adventitious disorder a sign of <s>vāta</s> and the others necessarily arises from disturbance of the body; but for some length of time that does not serve as an occasion for treatment of <s>vāta</s> and the others, as has been said: "There, wind born from trauma, generally vitiating the blood," and so on.

children.text: mānase'pi kāmādau doṣakopo bhavatyeva yaduktaṃ kāmaśokabhayādvāyur ityādi ||
children.translated_text: Even in a mental condition such as desire, aggravation of the <s>doṣa</s>s certainly occurs, as has been said: "From passion, grief, and fear, <s>vāyu</s>," and so on.
"Because the result is observed" means: because in all curable disorders a result in the form of relief is seen through treatment directed to <s>vāta</s> and the others.
Even in an adventitious disorder, because of its continuation over time, a result occurs through treatment of the <s>doṣa</s>s.

children.text: āgamācceti nāsti rogo vinā doṣair ityādi carake 'pyuktaṃ vikāro dhātuvaiṣamyam iti ||
children.translated_text: "And from authoritative tradition" means: because it is said, "There is no disease without the <s>doṣa</s>s," and so on; in <s>Caraka</s> too it is said, "Disorder is imbalance of the <s>dhātu</s>s (bodily constituents)."
Here he gives an example with "just as," and so on.

children.text: vikārajātamiti mahadādīni sapta ekādaśendriyāṇi pañcārthās tathā tadvikārāśca goghaṭādayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "The class of transformations" means the seven beginning with <s>mahat</s> (cosmic intellect), the eleven sense faculties, the five objects, and also their transformations, such as cows and pots.

children.text: viśvarūpeṇeti sthāvarādiviśvarūpatayā sattvarajastamasāmeva hi prakṛtirūpāṇāṃ mahadādi sarvaṃ pariṇāma iti sāṃkhyanayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "In manifold form" means in the form of manifold things such as immobile beings; for according to the <s>Sāṃkhya</s> doctrine, everything beginning with <s>mahat</s> is a transformation of <s>sattva</s>, <s>rajas</s>, and <s>tamas</s>, which themselves have the nature of <s>prakṛti</s> (primordial matter).
"In manifold form" means in forms such as fever, diarrhea, and wounds.
